Anthracnose.quote: sunken lesions, softening, and formation of viscous asexual conidia ranging from yellow to orange
Additional affected tissues include "twig blight" and "cane cankers characterized by tissue necrosis"
Dark brown lesions may develop on twigs and become surrounded by reproductive structures (acervuli), and reddish brown lesions can also occur on infected leaves

Blueberry_Leaf_Rust.quote: The disease first appears as small yellow (chlorotic) spots on the upper surface of young blueberry leaves. As the infection progresses the spots turn a reddish-purple color with a discrete yellow halo.

Botrytis_Blight.quote: Grayish spores form in masses on the blossoms
Infections progress from infected blossoms back into the woody tissues, creating twig lesions and potentially killing the supporting stems
the leaves will also develop brown lesions

Scorch.quote: Necrotic flowers and leaves will initially be brown, but later bleach to an ash gray color.
Young developing twigs may be killed outright
Infected bushes will have poor growth and fruit production, and may be killed
